title.narrative: Smart Paper Technology in Health PBF

description.narrative: 115 beneficiaries i.e. 100 health workers, 10 DHMT members and 5 Cordaid staff. 20 health facilities will benefit at large and 5 district in Eastern Uganda i.e. Bukwo, Kweni, Kapchorwa, Namayingo and Kalangala.

Cordaid is Uganda is currently applying its popular Results Based Financing (RBF) approach in the HEROs Project- an SRHR and SGBV adolescent focused project. Like for many other RBF interventions, one of the challenges currently faced is effective collection, management and timely utilization of bulky data. The Smart Paper Technology has demonstrated ability to address this challenge. Below are the specific gaps to be addressed. • Poor data availability from the health centres (disaggregated data on effective coverage) • Cumbersome and cost-intensive RBF data verification processes (internal and external) posing sustainability issues • Data alteration to influence RBF bonuses • Perverse incentives for the facilities to focus more on data management and reporting than quality of care to clients because of existing incentive mechanism and measurement approaches • Reactive approach of addressing gaps and inefficiencies in health delivery points, and forecasting mechanisms to proactively plan interventions • Duplication of efforts and financial resources to collect and report on data to different stakeholders • Lack of visibility of data quality and quality of care indicators (at all levels) • Lack of visibility of actions taken based on the data and continuous monitoring of intervention results (at all levels) • Lack of relevant data for decision-making due to the existing limitations of data management • Inadequate data collection, analysis/synthesis, communication and use of data at all levels • Shortage of skilled health workers, low retention rate and high data management burden • Labour-intensive and error-prone paper-based data management processes • Lack of attention to and poor data use culture and systems-wide approach in evidence-based decision-making • Lack of attention to quality-of-care indicators and necessary actions

Overall Objective: Through SPT, Cordaid will contribute to establishing a functional performance measurement and improvement system at selected health facilities and district levels, to systematically improve access, utilization and coverage, quality and efficiency of services in a sustainable manner and with a specific notion of vulnerable groups, such as adolescents, youth, women with a strong gender bias.
SO 1 (Short Term): Replace bulky paper based RBF data verification processes with a simpler and lighter digitalized option.
SO 2 (Short Term): Strengthen capacity of Health Facility and District Health Leadership teams to make timely data-based decisions.
SO 3 (long term/intermediate): Strengthen the health management information system (HMIS) for the continuum of care including Reproductive Maternal Neonatal, Child and Adolescent Health (RMNCAH) services. SO 3 (long term/intermediate): Contribute to the establishment of functional quality improvement system, across the health system
